correctness.rationale: The gamma moment formula yields exact Fourier coefficients and orthogonal input/output pairs. Uniform digamma differentiation proves n^{-1} bulk coefficients; an explicit n^{-beta}(1+|r|)^{beta-1} majorant controls the gamma interface. Dominated series, Riemann sums, and a uniform harmonic middle-zone estimate give all three regimes. Strict discrete concavity of g_beta gives the norm constant. The standalone diagnostic independently checked 88,784 finite identities/asymptotic sanity cases; finite tests are not used to justify infinite limits.

originality.rationale: The new statement is a complete sharp fixed-positive-degree-gap asymptotic in beta-weighted harmonic Bergman space. It identifies a singular gamma interface, a new critical index p_c=1/(1-beta), a two-sided logarithmic residue, and norm-versus-trace behavior. Closest primary works provide algebraic rank/coefficient results or different large-degree regimes; neither of the two complete published spectral comparisons states or directly subsumes the coalescing-gap limits. Novelty remains best-knowledge, not an independence or priority certification.

value.rationale: In a natural regime excluded by existing positive fixed-ratio spectral laws, the two rapidly growing powers nearly commute. The theorem quantifies this instability across all Schatten scales, identifies a sharp gamma-function norm and nonzero limiting trace norm, and proves a genuine bulk-versus-interface logarithmic phase transition. These are motivated spectral invariants of the same canonical Toeplitz family and not arbitrary finite parameter slices.
